chunks: Dāwūd ibn Isḥāq narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Fayḍ, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about mutʿah. He said: “Yes, if she is knowledgeable.”

I said: “May I be your ransom, what if she is not knowledgeable?” He said: “Then present it to her and tell her. If she accepts, then marry her. If she refuses and is not satisfied with your statement, then leave her. And beware of al-kawāshif, al-dawāʿī, al-baghāyā, and women with husbands.”
I said: “What are al-kawāshif?” He said: “Those who expose themselves, whose houses are known, and who are approached.”
I said: “Then al-dawāʿī?” He said: “Those who invite others to themselves and have become known for فساد.”
I said: “Then al-baghāyā?” He said: “Those known for zinā.”
I said: “Then women with husbands?” He said: “Those divorced contrary to the sunnah (prophetic tradition).”

key_terms.الدَّوَاعِيَ: women who call or invite others to themselves for immorality
key_terms.الْبَغَايَا: women known for prostitution or fornication
key_terms.الْكَوَاشِفَ: women who openly expose themselves and are publicly accessible
key_terms.الْمُطَلَّقَاتُ عَلَى غَيْرِ السُّنَّةِ: women divorced in a manner contrary to the sunnah (prophetic tradition)
key_terms.ذَوَاتَ الْأَزْوَاجِ: women who are considered to have husbands
key_terms.عَارِفَةً: knowledgeable about the matter and its ruling

ai.seo_question: What conditions and restrictions does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام mention for mutʿah marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning mutʿah and stipulates that the woman should understand the arrangement, or it should first be explained to her. It also warns against entering such a marriage with women publicly known for sexual corruption, and clarifies categories of women who are to be avoided, including those improperly divorced.
